scope: Source-level inventory of the finished application, including portable helpers. Runtime reachability and platform behavior are described in crypto-audit.md. This inventory is not an export classification or a binary scan.

features.name: Optional CrispCloud file and filename encryption
features.note: Existing nonce/ciphertext/tag wire format is preserved. The optional key is session-only and the envelope does not contain its derivation salt; new connection setup requires confirmation of the exact recovery mnemonic before activation. Native acceleration does not eliminate Dart crypto or make Apple builds OS-only.

features.name: Filen provider
features.note: Required provider; retain protocol compatibility. The production SDK uses the same injected host secure credential store as the app, verifies saved bytes before persistent legacy-file cleanup, and preserves durable legacy credentials in session mode. The standalone SDK CLI's default credential wrapping is not a substitute for host secure storage.

algorithms: HKDF / Argon2 key derivation for v3 accounts (hkdf, argon2)
rust_engine.note: Optional per-connection engine (Dart remains available). Same protocol and algorithms as the Dart provider; RustCrypto crates (aes, cbc, cipher, pbkdf2, hmac, sha1, sha2, md-5) and TLS through reqwest with rustls; standard algorithms only.

features.name: Internxt provider
features.note: Required provider. Published legacy modes are preserved for interoperability; standard/public does not mean every construction provides modern authenticated encryption. See residual risks in crypto-audit.md.

algorithms: AES-256-CBC legacy text with EVP_BytesToKey/MD5 (cbc, md-5)
rust_engine.note: Optional per-connection engine. Logs in through Internxt's keyless compatibility flow, so no OpenPGP keys are generated in Rust. RustCrypto crates (aes, cbc, cipher, pbkdf2, hmac, sha1, sha2, md-5) and TLS through reqwest with rustls; standard algorithms only.

features.name: Cryptomator format helpers
features.note: Format primitives and authenticated config/header parsing, not a complete cloud vault filesystem.

features.name: VeraCrypt helpers and desktop CLI
features.note: Bundled parser supports a limited set of volume headers. Full mounting is a separately installed desktop executable and unavailable in App Store/mobile builds. CRC is a format check, not cryptographic authentication.

features.name: Transport, accounts, and remote storage
algorithms: SMB signing and SMB3 encryption requirements through the default libsmb2 transport or an explicitly selected native Rust wrapper
features.note: libsmb2 remains the default SMB transport. Strict Rust selection requires the optional native bridge; Auto falls back only when native loading or bridge initialization is unavailable, before constructing a transport session. Authentication, network, signing, encryption and transfer failures do not trigger backend fallback. Signing remains required and encryption is required by default; these source-level policy checks do not establish every negotiated algorithm or server/platform behavior. GUI credentials use the configured SecureStorage backend. CLI credentials remain in its separate plaintext YAML configuration, with mode 0600 applied on non-Windows writes; the native wrapper adds no credential store. An external CRISP_SMB_LIBRARY selection requires separate verification of the actual library bytes. Review negotiated algorithms, native dependency sources and packaged artifacts for each resolved release; TLS is not the complete app crypto scope.

features.name: Application credential storage and App Lock gates
algorithms: AES-256-GCM credential values with 96-bit nonces and 128-bit tags
PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256: 600000 iterations for new credential vaults; complete iterationless legacy vaults use 100000
Version 2 encrypted record envelope binding each new value to its storage key
Legacy App Lock verifier: 10000-round SHA-256 salt/PIN loop, separate from the credential-vault KDF
implementations: Existing native crypto provider selection and WebCrypto browser provider
flutter_secure_storage platform backend; macOS data-protection keychain by default
Security.framework SecItem operations scoped to an explicit macOS file-keychain reference and com.crispcloud.credentials.v1 service
Transactional native JSON file backend with OS locks and atomic replacement
features.note: PR26 follow-up: configured-store failures are explicit, not an automatic backend switch; settings distinguish active/pending selection and guard App Lock. Startup recovery can regrant access only to the same existing configured macOS keychain, verified before bookmark replacement, and then retries its original policy gate. A missing existing vault blocks startup. Version-3 selections carry an explicit fresh-setup/authenticated-switch creation grant, consumed through a verified write before initialization and never automatically restored after failure; version-2 selections imply no grant. Preference serialization is not cross-process compare-and-swap. Session-only does not import or delete persistent legacy credentials. File-vault metadata is validated before KDF work, with a 2000000-iteration ceiling; new version 2 credential values reject cross-key substitution, while legacy unbound values remain readable until rewritten. Native transactions do not imply browser cross-tab atomicity or whole-vault anti-rollback protection. Custom keychain creation refuses occupied/reserved paths and retains security-scoped access without global default/search-list setters. File/session backends require foreground availability and do not unlock unattended workers. This entry does not grant a new export classification or an OS-only Apple exemption.

features.name: Archive password compatibility
algorithms: Traditional PKWARE ZipCrypto legacy stream cipher (read only)
WinZip AES-128/192/256-CTR read; AES-256 AE-2 write
WinZip PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 (1000 iterations) and truncated HMAC-SHA1
7z AES-256-CBC read/write with published format-specific SHA-256 KDF (not PBKDF2)
RAR3/4 AES-128-CBC read with published format-specific SHA-1 KDF (262144 rounds, not PBKDF2)
RAR5 AES-256-CBC read with HMAC-SHA256 PBKDF2-style key derivation and format checksum/password checks
features.note: Reachable through the portable archive viewer and workspace, including mobile. Exact source paths, archive hashes and MIT licenses are recorded in crypto-dependencies.md. No older RAR1.x/2.x cipher was found in the supported encrypted paths. Published availability and international-standard recognition are separate claims; this finding is not an Apple/BIS classification or automatic CCATS conclusion. Existing format compatibility is retained.

features.name: KeePass KDBX database viewing and editing
algorithms: AES-256-CBC with PKCS#7 padding or ChaCha20 outer database encryption
KeePass AES-KDF or Argon2d/Argon2id versions 0x10/0x13 through PointyCastle
SHA-256 password/key-file composition and SHA-256/SHA-512 format key derivation
KDBX4 HMAC-SHA-256 header and block authentication, including the terminal block
KDBX3 encrypted start bytes, SHA-256 block hashes and encrypted header hash
Salsa20 or ChaCha20 inner protected values
Random.secure fresh seeds, KDF salts, stream keys and IVs on save
implementations: Vendored KPassLib 1.1.2 at upstream 81d51d9f3575f72136441ea5a271f6748e3ca77c with recorded local format/preservation patches
Default pure-Dart CryptoDart engine; Argon2 adapter uses already-resolved PointyCastle 4.0.0
Existing crypto 3.0.7 hash/HMAC implementations; no new native KPassLib binary
features.note: New confidentiality workflow for existing KDBX 3.0/3.1/4.0/4.1 databases on native and web. Group management, entry moves, protected custom-field edits and complete history restoration use the same encrypted session. Preserves existing cipher/KDF costs and untouched XML/history/attachments, with bounded input/KDF work and pre-mutation structure/size checks. Source-bound saves and lock checkpoints contain ciphertext only; no persistent master credentials or plaintext recovery copies. App does not load upstream FFI engine or expose runtime cipher plugins. This is not Apple-OS-only cryptography. No claim that every algorithm or construction is internationally standardized, no new legal classification, and no post-feature Apple questionnaire result; documentation review remains pending.

features.name: Documents, backups, and transitive crypto
algorithms: PDF password protection (legacy RC4 and AES variants)
Office AES-CBC password encryption and SHA-family derivation
encrypted account backup and profile data
features.note: Bundled source contains additional compatibility crypto. Inventory the dependency graph and native archive/SMB sources; this list is not an assertion that every algorithm is reachable on every platform or fully audited.

features.name: KeePass database viewer/editor
algorithms: AES-256-CBC, ChaCha20 and Salsa20 (KDBX 3/4 payload and inner stream)
features.note: Vendored MIT kpasslib (pinned source, local preservation/web patches). Opens and saves the user's own KDBX files with the user's master key; standard published algorithms only.

features.name: FTP over TLS
algorithms: TLS on FTP control and data connections (explicit/implicit FTPS) via Dart SecurityContext with certificate validation
features.note: Vendored MIT ftpconnect 2.0.10 runtime; platform TLS only.

features.name: Encrypted archive creation
algorithms: ZIP: WinZip AES-256 with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 (package:archive ZipEncoder)
7z: AES-256 with iterated SHA-256 key derivation, optional header encryption (koni_sevenz writer)
features.note: User-requested password-protected archives.

features.name: E-book DRM detection
algorithms: none: encryption.xml and Kindle DRM markers are detected and such books are refused
features.note: No DRM removal or decryption is implemented.

features.name: Ebook identifiers, local annotations, and reader sessions
algorithms: SHA-256 publication identifier suffixes, exact-book annotation keys, and prose-edit fingerprints
features.note: The digests identify source versions and detect stale prose edits; they do not encrypt books or annotations. Local annotations use SharedPreferences. The random session identifier scopes reader bridge messages alongside host source/origin checks. CRC-32 is a format check, not authentication. The portable Linux search/bookmark/appearance extension introduces no additional cipher or key derivation.

features.name: EPUB and Kindle font obfuscation compatibility
algorithms: IDPF font obfuscation: SHA-1 of the whitespace-stripped publication identifier, repeating XOR over the first 1040 font bytes
Adobe EPUB font obfuscation: UUID-derived 16-byte key, repeating XOR over the first 1024 font bytes
MOBI FONT record obfuscation: record-provided repeating XOR key over 1024 bytes for a 16-byte key, otherwise 1040 bytes
implementations: WebCrypto SHA-1 and JavaScript deobfuscators in foliate-js
Vendored Kindling fonts.rs SHA-1 implementation and deobfuscate
features.note: These compatibility paths are reachable for supported font resources. They do not provide general ebook DRM decryption. Unknown EPUB encryption is rejected; Kindling's native bridge also rejects rights.xml and unrecognized EncryptionMethod values. The Dart document retains original obfuscated bytes, and Kindling's output FONT records use compression without XOR obfuscation. The metadata-only browser worker does not decode fonts.

features.name: Bundled ebook ZIP cryptography and rejected password paths
algorithms: Bundled zip.js/SJCL: AES-128/192/256 in WinZip CTR mode
Bundled zip.js/SJCL: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 (1000 iterations), HMAC-SHA1 truncated to 10 bytes
Traditional PKWARE ZipCrypto present in zip.js and Rust zip source
features.note: The pinned JavaScript asset contains these implementations even though the ebook loader rejects every encrypted ZIP entry before getData and never supplies a password. Its PBKDF2 has a WebCrypto path and SJCL fallback; its unused encryption code contains crypto.getRandomValues plus a Math.random-based fallback, which is not treated as a secure reachable app RNG. The Dart EPUB container independently rejects password-encrypted ZIP flags. Native conversion uses passwordless Rust zip 9.3.0 reads, which reject encrypted entries; default features and aes-crypto are disabled in the reviewed manifests. Rust ZipCrypto source remains in the dependency, so disabled AES is not a claim that the dependency source is crypto-free. No ebook password-decryption UI or password-encryption output is added. Existing archive-viewer password support is covered separately.

features.name: Kindle conversion and browser metadata engine
algorithms: MD5 for Kindle format metadata: EXTH 542 title hash prefixes, native export identifiers and font-signature ordering
SHA-1 and XOR font compatibility in native EPUB conversion, as listed separately
features.note: Kindling 0.46.2 contains full MD5 implementations; changing a title reaches md5_first4 in the native and browser metadata byte API. These hashes are format fields, not authentication or encryption. Metadata rewriting rejects nonzero PalmDOC encryption and DRM EXTH 401/402/403 in either primary or KF8 sections before output. The browser bridge sets doc_type and cover_image to None, so it does not invoke font conversion or embedded source-ZIP extraction. The Wasm lock retains ahash 0.8.12, getrandom 0.3.4/0.4.3, rand 0.8.8, rand_core 0.6.4 and wasm-bindgen 0.2.121; getrandom's wasm_js feature permits compilation of the broader dependency graph. The inspected bundled Wasm has zero host imports, and metadata_runtime.js rejects modules with imports. This establishes no browser RNG/crypto imports for that artifact, not absence of internal MD5 or an audit of every dependency. External/prebuilt native-library or custom worker overrides require separate artifact provenance; a version/ABI string alone is not a content hash. No export-policy classification or Apple approval is established by this source inventory.

features.name: Ebook reading-data exchange, library identities, and shared reader hosts
algorithms: SHA-256 of exact publication bytes, canonical reading-data snapshots and source/attachment catalog identities
Existing Dart Random.secure 24-byte reader session identifiers
implementations: Optional system WebKitGTK 4.1 on Linux; existing platform WebViews or the browser elsewhere
features.note: The added SHA-256 uses bind data to exact content and renderer versions, detect stale import previews, and derive catalog IDs; they are not signatures, MACs, encryption or access grants. Reading-data exports are plain UTF-8 JSON without source paths, account metadata or credentials. Local sidecars and the library index use SharedPreferences; the index can retain exact persistent account/root/file references but resolves authentication separately. In-process locks and stale-instance checks do not establish cross-process or browser-tab transactions. Shared appearance controls accept bounded numbers and allowlisted choices, not arbitrary CSS or scripts. The Linux CMake target links system GTK3/gmodule and optional epoxy, dynamically loads libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0 at version 2.48.4 or newer, and copies no WebKit runtime into the bundle. Its ephemeral host requires the WebKit process sandbox and uses the existing session loopback assets, CSP and sanitized book frames. No new production Dart dependency, cipher implementation, KDF or credential store is added by this increment. Installed system WebKit and transitive TLS/crypto implementations, finished binaries and distribution decisions remain outside this bounded technical source review. The shared search controller serializes Foliate iterators and suppresses canceled search overlays; section resource cleanup and explicit reading-state discard add no cryptographic or network capability. The optional Linux host now installs a separate, system-WebKit-linked readiness executable. The application/plugin remain dynamically linked only to their prior system host libraries, while the helper loads a fixed no-network document under the enabled WebKit sandbox before any publication view is created. The host bounds startup, closes inherited descriptors, suppresses helper output/core dumps and cleans the owned child group before reaping; no source path, publication data or credentials are passed as helper arguments. No runner policy or sandbox setting is relaxed.

features.name: Legacy Word conversion and retained signature evidence
algorithms: ZIP format CRC checks through the existing archive dependency; no signature validation or decryption implementation
features.note: Bounded DOC/DOT parsing and separate DOCX/DOCM output. Original signature bytes are inert evidence; converted output does not claim the original signature validity. The parser never executes VBA or embedded objects.

features.name: Retained tool staging and conditional publication
algorithms: Existing SHA-256 content fingerprints and OS-backed private staging identifiers
features.note: Digests bind retained copies and reviewed publication/recovery inputs. No new cipher, password decryption path or distribution decision is introduced.

features.name: FictionBook conversion and bounded serialization
algorithms: Existing Dart crypto SHA-256 for a fallback document identifier derived from title and authors
features.note: Pure Dart EPUB-to-FB2/FBZ conversion writes a separate in-memory output. It validates the source, refuses signed/encrypted input and non-representable active/foreign/media content, confines packaged resource paths, bounds output and image counts, and validates emitted local links. The fallback hash is a format identifier, not authentication, encryption or an exact-content identity. Embedded raster resources use Base64; FBZ uses the existing passwordless archive writer. No new cryptographic implementation, key handling, credential store, network destination or native dependency is added.
